pairs.why: Both use quiet concentric rings behind the player with a brighter centre glow, so staging and detail don't separate them.
A has a few large quiet shapes (sand mound, one shell, two coins, few bubbles), while B adds extra pebbles and more small bubbles that the real card's sparse seabed lacks.
A's soft floor with one large shadow is quieter, while B's hard-edged slab corner adds a shape the real card's smooth curved ledge doesn't have.
Both put the map on soft tone-on-tone diagonal stripes with no props, matching the real card equally.
A keeps the desert to a few large shapes (mesa, sky, track, one tuft), while B scatters rocks and bushes around the track, which is busier than the real cards' environments.
B's rings stay an even quiet tone-on-tone field like the real cards, while A adds a hot yellow glow behind the boot that competes with it.
B stands on a smooth, simple dune with nothing else, like the real cards' plain ground, while A scatters rocks and craters on grey moon ground.
A shows the wagon whole in a calm field with a dirt path, like the real cards' wide quiet scenes, while B is cropped tight with a blurred background and a big prop-like tongue.
